executionPlan: Added procedural world materials and a sky (world-space triplanar textures drawn on canvases at runtime), dusk lighting with soft shadows, and instanced visual-only decor generated from the layout. Layout, colliders and camera code were not touched. Compared before and after on the real GPU: before was the production build of the original M3 tree, after was the production build of this tree, plus screenshot, entry-frame, performance and hero pixel tooling.
summary: The campus now reads as a dusk technology campus: sky gradient with ridge and stars, fog to the horizon colour, a warm key light with soft PCF shadows (also on the avatar), textured grass, paving, gravel, plaster, stone and metal, lit windows and neon trim, readable project screens, 3D trees and lamps, and soft light pools. Lint, 488 tests and build exit 0, / is 125 kB, draw calls dropped from 117 to 56, and rAF p95 is 16.7 ms. Not met cleanly: the hero cannot be proven pixel-identical because it animates (static pixels are identical, 0 of 1.21M), the entry fade now starts after a roughly 45 ms first-frame compile, and the entry loading pause grew to about 215 ms.

criteria.criterion: Before and after screenshot pairs at 1440x900 on the real GPU, from spawn, at each destination forecourt and entrance, inside each hall, and at the beacon, show a coherent dusk campus: a sky gradient and distance fog instead of flat black, warm-to-cool dusk key and fill lighting with soft shadows on the avatar and buildings, ground that reads as paving, grass and paths instead of one flat colour, buildings with finished materials and trim, green-cyan accents consistent with the site's terminal palette, readable signs, and trees and props that no longer look like single boxes; no surface is overexposed or clipped (the beacon pad and tower doorway frame read as lit installations, not flat white-cyan slabs).
criteria.evidence: 11 pairs plus the beacon in the shot directory (before-* from the original M3 production build, after-* from this tree), 1440x900. Each pair was inspected; the sky has a navy gradient, a warm horizon afterglow band, a ridge line and stars, with fog meeting the horizon colour. The warm key (-9,10,-13) with cool fill gives soft PCF shadows on buildings, trees and the avatar. Ground is textured grass with a cliff texture on the ravine sides, paving tiles, gravel paths with curbs. Buildings have plaster and ashlar stone, dark steel trim, lit windows, door jambs, roofs with ridge caps and rooftop plant. Signs are unchanged and readable; project screens carry XECSUITE, NEWSSTOCKS.LIVE, APEX MIND, SKILLS, EXPERIENCE and CONTACT. Trees are noise-displaced leaf clumps and conifers on tapered trunks; there are lamps, planters with shrubs, benches with backs, rocks and a pine line beyond the hedge. Clip check: 0 percent of pixels at or above 250 in all channels in every after shot, at most 0.19 percent with a channel at 254 or more. The beacon pad is a dark plate with glowing ring and corner marks; the tower door frame is neon with edge falloff inside a dark steel surround. Still flat: the lab floor strip and some neon strips are uniform cyan or green, though no longer white. Extra shots: ravine edge, terrace, west and east fields.

ASSETS.md has a new section: zero asset files, procedural textures, about 11 KB gzip extra JS (1,291,564 to 1,302,567), about 10 MB GPU texture memory; far under 8 MB.

assumptions: Quality is resolved with resolveQuality('auto') in GameScene because the settings panel does not exist yet; before this it was hard-coded to the low preset with no shadows. Mobile and 4-core devices stay on low (no shadows) and were not measured.
Shadow depth warm-up uses the real key light borrowed for two off-screen passes; this relies on three r163 internals and should be re-checked on a three upgrade.
The original M3 production build in the game-dev scratch directory (b-main) was used as the before baseline; its sources equal the worktree except for my files.
Project screen titles come from the portfolio's own project names; I did not invent technology names.
Headless Chrome with the Mac GPU stands in for a real display; the GPU model was not read.
decisionsProposed: World materials sample procedural textures in world space (triplanar onBeforeCompile) so every block size and rotation keeps the same texel density and everything can be instanced by material.
GameScene now takes the quality preset from resolveQuality('auto'); a later settings panel should replace that one call.
The Canvas resets renderer.shadowMap on every prop change, so WorldView re-asserts it each frame while the game is mounted.
lessonsProposed: The R3F Canvas re-applies its shadows setting (off) on any prop change; assert shadowMap.enabled in a per-frame hook, and set it before any compile.

Program cache keys include light counts, shadow-light counts, fog, shadow flags and render-target colour management: compile in the exact state the game draws in (hide the hero lights, include the avatar clone), never into a render target, or the first game frame stalls.
gl.shadowMap.render cannot be called outside a render; borrow the real shadow light into a throwaway scene and render twice through a camera that looks away.
Additive decals must use renderOrder after the surfaces they lie on, otherwise later transparent surfaces overwrite them.
For a time-based fade, any first-frame compile eats part of the fade; count new programs per frame (gl.info.programs) when judging entry smoothness.
An animating hero cannot be compared pixel for pixel; use a static-region mask and a baseline-versus-baseline noise floor.
